architectural_units.name: Security Service
architectural_units.description: The Security Service is composed exclusively of certain functionalities of the Traefik tool, acting as a reverse proxy and load balancer.

architectural_units.name: Traefik
architectural_units.description: Traefik is a modern reverse proxy and load balancer designed to manage incoming and outgoing HTTP and HTTPS traffic in container-based applications.

architectural_units.name: System Service
architectural_units.description: The System Service serves the web application using React and Next.js, managing the core application logic.

architectural_units.name: Next.js
architectural_units.description: Next.js is a framework for building web applications that offers additional structure, features, and optimizations.

architectural_units.name: React
architectural_units.description: React is an open-source JavaScript library designed to build user interfaces efficiently and flexibly.

architectural_units.name: Data Service
architectural_units.description: The Data Service provides the relational database for storing application data.

architectural_units.name: PostgreSQL
architectural_units.description: PostgreSQL provides the relational database for storing application data.

architectural_units.name: Prisma
architectural_units.description: Prisma is an ORM tool designed to simplify database access and management in Node.js and TypeScript applications.

architectural_units.name: Docker
architectural_units.description: Docker is a software containerization platform used to manage the execution of containers for the services.
Security Service (Traefik) manages the routing of HTTP and HTTPS requests to the System Service (Next.js).
System Service (Next.js) communicates with the Data Service (PostgreSQL) using Prisma ORM.

patterns.name: Microservices
patterns.description: The architecture implemented for the development of the Revivack project system is an architecture based on microservices.

patterns.name: Component-Based
patterns.description: The Component-Based pattern focuses on building the user interface by creating independent and reusable components.

patterns.name: Observer Pattern
patterns.description: The Observer pattern establishes a one-to-many relationship between objects, where a subject maintains a list of observers.

patterns.name: Singleton Pattern
patterns.description: The Singleton pattern ensures that a class has only one instance and provides a global access point to that instance.
